If Hán and Wèi fight and defeat Qín,
then half their troops are lost,
The borders of the four directions are not defended;
to fight and not win,
then the state is already in imminent danger of destruction.
Therefore,
this is why Hán Wèi considered it important to fight Qín,
and took lightly becoming its subjects.
Now, Qín's attack on Qí is different:
it doubles the territory of Hán and Wèi,
passes through the roads of Wèi and Jìnyáng,
goes by the dangerous pass of Kàngfǔ,
where carriages cannot travel side by side,
and cavalry cannot ride abreast.
If a hundred men guard the pass,
a thousand men dare not pass.
Even if Qín desires to advance deeply,
it will look back in alarm,
fearing that Hán and Wèi will plot against its rear.
Therefore,
they frighten with doubtful and empty threats,
arrogant and haughty, yet dare not advance.
To not deeply consider that Qín can do nothing to Qí,
and to desire to face west and serve them,
this is a miscalculation by your ministers.
Now, there is no name of serving Qín,
but there is the reality of a strong state,
therefore, I wish that Your Majesty would pay a little attention to planning."
The King of Qí said,
"Good."
Sū Qín 蘇秦 persuaded King Mǐn 閔 of Qí 齊, saying:
"I have heard:
He who delights in striking first in warfare invites worry;
He who delights in inciting resentment when making alliances invites isolation.
To arise after others
is to have support;
To avoid incurring resentment from afar
is to seize the opportune moment.
Thus, the saying goes:
'When a qílì 騏驥 (fine horse) declines,
a dull horse precedes it;
When Mèng Bēn 孟賁 (a strong warrior) tires,
a woman overcomes him.'
That the dull horse and the woman do not have bones and strength like
the excellent horse and Mèng Bēn,
why is this?
Because they arise after the others and have support.
I have heard:
In the way of warfare,
without a guiding principle,
even with a million soldiers,
it is like being inside a hall;
even with generals like Chāng Hé 閶闔 and Wú Qǐ 吳起,
they can be captured within a house;
a thousand-foot city wall
can be taken down between cups and plates;
a hundred-foot siege ramp
can be broken on the mat.
Therefore, the sounds of bells, drums, *yú*, *sè*, and pipes never cease,
the land can be expanded and desires can be fulfilled;
harmonious music and the laughter of actors and musicians are never lacking,
the feudal lords can be brought together on the same day.
Therefore, those who are good at becoming kings
lie in exhausting the world while they themselves relax,
throwing the world into chaos while they themselves remain at peace.
If the feudal lords have no established plans,
then the state will have no lasting worries.
How do we know this is so?
In the past, the King of Wèi possessed a territory of a thousand *lǐ*,
with 360,000 armored soldiers,
and followed twelve feudal lords to pay homage to the Son of Heaven,
in order to plot against Qín in the west.
Qín was afraid,
unable to sleep peacefully,
and finding no taste in food.
Wèi Yāng strategized to the King of Qín, saying:
'Why doesn't Your Majesty send me to see the King of Wèi?
Then I will surely request the north of Wèi.'
The King of Qín agreed.
Wèi Yāng met the King of Wèi,
and said:
'Your Majesty's achievements are great!
Your orders are carried out throughout the world!
However, among the twelve feudal lords,
aside from Sòng and Wèi, there are only Zōu, Lǔ, Chén, and Cài.
These are indeed the states that Your Majesty can whip and drive;
was not sufficient to rule the world.
It would be better to take Yān 燕 to the north,
and attack Qí 齊 to the east,
then Zhào 趙 would surely follow.
Take Qín 秦 to the west,
and attack Chǔ 楚 to the south,
then Hán 韓 would surely follow.
If Your Majesty has the ambition to attack Qí 齊 and Chǔ 楚,
and the desire to unite the world,
then the kingly enterprise will be realized.
Your Majesty should first adopt the attire of a king,
and then plan against Qí 齊 and Chǔ 楚."
The King of Wèi 魏王 approved of this,
therefore he expanded the public palace in his person,
made crimson robes,
built nine-tiered pillars,
and followed the Seven Stars banner.
This was the position of the Son of Heaven,
and the King of Wèi 魏王 occupied it.
Thereupon, Qí 齊 and Chǔ 楚 were angered,
the feudal lords fled to Qí 齊,
the people of Qí 齊 attacked Wèi 魏,
killed the crown prince,
and overturned his army of one hundred thousand.
At that time,
the King of Qín 秦王 received the land west of the Yellow River with folded hands.
Therefore, when Wèi Yāng 衛鞅 first consulted with the King of Qín 秦王,
the plans agreed upon before he left the mat
Furthermore, the general of Wèi had already been captured by Qí.
Before the ramming towers could be deployed,
the area outside the Xī River had already fallen to Qín.
This is what your servant means by capturing generals inside chambers and taking cities between cups and tables, defeating enemies on the mats in the north in halls."
King Huái of Chǔ sent the Pillar of the State, Zhāo Yáng, to lead troops to attack Wèi.
He gained eight cities
and then moved his troops to attack Qí.
King Mǐn of Qí was worried about this.
Chén Zhěn said,
"Your Majesty, do not worry,
allow me to make him withdraw."
He immediately went to see Zhāo Yáng at the army camp,
bowed twice,
and congratulated him on his victorious battle,
rising and asking,
"May I ask about the laws of Chǔ:
For overturning an army and killing a general,
what is the official position and title?"
Zhāo Yáng said,
"The official position is Senior Pillar of the State,
the title is Senior Holder of the Guī Scepter."
Chén Zhěn said,
"What is more esteemed than this?"
Zhāo Yáng said:
"Only the Prime Minister."
Zhěn said,
"The Prime Minister is esteemed!
It is not the same as establishing two Lìngyǐn!
Your servant dares to make an analogy for you, my lord.
May I?
In Chǔ, there was a man offering a sacrifice.
He gifted his fellow lodgers one cup of wine.
The lodgers said to one another:
"There is not enough for several people to drink,
But there is enough for one person to drink.
Let us draw snakes on the ground,
Whoever finishes first drinks the wine."
One person finished his snake first.
He drew the wine near and was about to drink it.
Then he held the cup in his left hand,
And drew on the ground with his right hand,
Saying:
"I can add feet to it."
Before the feet were finished,
Another person completed his snake.
He snatched the cup from him,
Saying:
"Snakes inherently have no feet,
How can you add feet to it?"
And then he drank the wine.
The one who drew feet on the snake,
In the end lost his wine.
Now you, my lord, attacked Wèi,
Defeated armies and killed generals,
And obtained eight cities.
Ér yòu yí bīng gōng Qí,
Qi was very afraid of Gong.
With this, to be known as a capable ruler is sufficient!
The crown on top is not something to be valued further!
To fight without fail and not know when to stop,
one's body will die,
one's title will be taken away,
and it would be like drawing a snake with feet."
Zhāo Yáng thought this was right
and led the army away.
Sū Qín went to Chu.
The ancestry of Chu,
came from Emperor Zhuānxū.
During the time of Emperor Kù and Gāoxīn, they were the grand administrators,
named Zhùróng.
Their descendants served King Wén of Zhōu.
During the time of King Chéng of Zhōu,
they elevated the descendants of those who were diligent and meritorious under Wén and Wǔ,
and enfeoffed Xióng Yì in the Chu lands among the barbarians,
with the fields of a viscount,
with the surname Qiān,
and greatly gained the harmony of the people between the Jiāng and Hàn rivers.
When it came to Xióng Tōng,
he sent an envoy to follow the people to Zhōu,
requesting to elevate his title.
Zhōu did not listen.
Xióng Tōng was angry,
and then he established himself as King Wǔ.
Speaking to King Wēi of Chǔ, he said:
"Chǔ
is the most powerful state in the world;
Your Majesty
is the most virtuous ruler in the world.
To the west, you have Qiánzhōng and Wū Commandery;
to the east, you have Xià Prefecture and Hǎiyáng;
to the south, you have Dòngtíng and Cāngwú;
to the north, you have Xíng Pass and Xúnyáng.
Your territory spans over five thousand *lǐ*,
with a million soldiers in armor,
a thousand chariots,
ten thousand horses,
and grain sufficient for ten years.
These are the resources for hegemony!
With Chǔ's strength
and Your Majesty's virtue,
no one in the world can match you.
Now, if you turn west and serve Qín,
then all the feudal lords will turn west and pay homage at the Zhāngtái Palace!
What Qín fears most
is Chǔ.
If Chǔ is strong, then Qín is weak;
if Qín is strong, then Chǔ is weak.
Their situations cannot both stand;
therefore, in planning for Your Majesty,
nothing is better than to ally with others to isolate Qín.
If Your Majesty does not follow the policy of alliance,
Qín will certainly raise two armies:
One army will emerge from Wǔ Guān,
and the other will descend upon Qián Zhōng.
Then Yān and Yǐng will be shaken!
Your servant has heard:
Govern it before it is in chaos,
Act on it before it exists.
To worry about calamity only after it arrives,
Then there is no time left!
Therefore, I wish Your Majesty to consider this carefully early.
If Your Majesty can truly listen to me,
I request that I may order the states east of the mountains (Shān Dōng),
To offer the tribute of the four seasons,
In order to receive Your Majesty’s clear commands;
To entrust the altars of soil and grain,
To honor the ancestral temples,
To train the soldiers and encourage the troops,
To be used by Your Majesty.
Therefore, to follow the alliance (cóng hé) makes one a Chǔ king,
To form the vertical alliance (héng chéng) makes one a Qín emperor.
Now, to abandon the enterprise of a hegemon or king,
And have the reputation of serving others,
I venture to say Your Majesty should not adopt this.
For Qín,
is a nation of tigers and wolves,
It has a heart to swallow all under Heaven.
Qín,
The greatest enemy in the world
is that the strategists all desire to cede the land of the feudal lords to serve Qín.
This is what is called "nurturing an enemy and serving a foe,"
a great act of rebellion and disloyalty,
nothing is greater than this.
Therefore, if one follows alliance, the feudal lords cede land to serve Chǔ;
if one follows horizontal alliance, then Chǔ cedes land to serve Qín.
These two policies are far apart,
where does Your Majesty stand between the two?
Therefore, the king of my humble state of Zhào sent me to offer a foolish plan
and present a clear agreement,
awaiting Your Majesty's command."
The King of Chǔ said,
"Good.
I will respectfully support the altars of the state and follow."
After King Xiāng of Chǔ made peace with Qín,
he was no longer worried about trouble from Qín,
so he and his four sons indulged in extravagance.
Zhuāng Xīn advised him, but he would not listen,
so Xīn left for Zhào.
Later, Qín indeed conquered Yān and Yǐng,
and King Xiāng then summoned Xīn to apologize to him.
Zhuāng Xīn said,
"I have heard a proverb that says:
'It is not too late to look for a dog after seeing a rabbit;
it is not too late;
it is not too late to repair the fold after losing a sheep;
it is not too late.'
Your servant has heard:
Tāng and Wǔ became kings with a hundred *lǐ* of territory,
while Jié and Zhòu perished despite possessing the entire empire.
Now, although the state of Chǔ is small,
if we eliminate the excessive and supplement the deficient,
it still encompasses a thousand *lǐ*,
how can it be merely a hundred *lǐ*!
Has Your Majesty not seen the dragonfly?
With six legs and four wings,
it flies freely between heaven and earth,
stooping to peck at mosquitoes (*wén'ǎi*) and gnats for food,
and looking up to receive white dew to drink,
thinking itself free from worry,
and having no strife with others.
It does not know that a five-foot-tall child
is about to prepare sticky glue on silk threads,
and place it forty *rèn* above,
so that it becomes food for ants.
The dragonfly is a small creature,
the yellow sparrow is also thus!
It pecks at white grains below,
perches on lush trees above,
flapping its wings energetically,
thinking itself free from worry,
and having no business with others.
It does not know that the sons and grandsons of nobles
hold a slingshot in their left hand
and grasp a pellet in their right,
He used his cheek as an arrowhead.
He painted nests on lush trees,
In the evening, he seasoned (food) with sour and salty flavors.
The yellow sparrow is but a small creature;
Cài Shènghóu indulged in these things!
He traveled south to the high banks (of the river),
He climbed north to Mount Wūshān,
He drank from the streams of the Rú River,
He ate the fish of the Xiāng River waves,
He pillowed his head on a young concubine on the left,
He embraced a favored woman on the right,
And galloped with them in the midst of Gāo and Cài,
And did not take state affairs seriously.
He did not know that Fūzǐ Fā had just received orders from King Xuān,
And bound himself with red silk cords to meet with him.
Cài Shènghóu concerned himself with petty matters;
The king indulged in these things!
With Lord Zuǒzhōu on the left,
And Lord Xiàhóu on the right,
Eating the millet of allotted salaries,
And carrying the gold of the square treasury,
Galloping with them in the midst of the Yúnmèng marshes,
And did not take the empire and the state seriously.
He did not know that Lord Rǎng had just received orders from the King of Qín,
To fill up the inner areas of the Mǐn River,
And throw himself outside the Mǐn River barrier.”
King Xiāng, hearing this,
His body trembled,
Thereupon, he held the *gui* tablet and presented it to Zhuāng Xīn,
and consulted with him about Qín,
later recovering the land north of the Huai River.
A man of Chǔ used a weak bow and a small arrow to shoot down a returning goose.
King Xiāng of Chǔ summoned him and asked about it,
to which he replied by comparing Qín, Yān, Zhào, and Wèi to birds,
in order to provoke the King's anger,
saying:
"The late king was deceived by Qín,
and died as a guest in a foreign land,
the resentment is immense!
Now, even a commoner has the ambition to avenge against a ruler of ten thousand chariots,
Zǐ Xū and Bái Gōng are examples of this.
Now, Chǔ's territory spans five thousand *li*,
with a million armored soldiers,
still enough to leap about in the middle of the fields.
Yet it sits passively and accepts subjugation,
I, your subject, humbly believe this is something that Your Majesty should not accept."
King Xiāng then resumed the policy of a vertical alliance to attack Qín.
Once the six states had united in a vertical alliance,
Sū Qín became the head of the vertical alliance.
He reported to Zhào,
and Marquis Sù of Zhào enfeoffed Sū Qín as Lord Wǔ'ān.
Thereupon, he threw the letter of vertical alliance at Qín,
and for more than fifteen years, Qín did not dare to peep its soldiers beyond the Hángǔ Pass.
Zhāng Yí advocated the horizontal alliance for Qín.
Qín wanted to attack Wèi,
and first defeated Hán,
Yóu the commissioner had the army behead eighty thousand men,
and the feudal lords were greatly frightened.
Thereupon Yí came to persuade the King of Wèi.
He said to the King of Wèi:
"In the time of Duke Xiào of Qín,
Gōngsūn Yāng requested to attack Wèi,
saying:
'Wèi is situated in the narrow and strategic pass of the mountains,
with its western capital at Ānyì,
bordering Qín by the river,
and exclusively enjoying the benefits of the area east of the mountains.
If they benefit, they will invade Qín to the west;
if they are weak, they will seize land to the east.
Now, because Your Majesty is wise and sagacious,
the state relies on this to prosper,
it is appropriate to attack Wèi at this time.
If Wèi is not friendly to Qín,
they will certainly move eastward.
If they move eastward, they will rely on the strength of the mountains and rivers,
and face eastward to control the feudal lords.
This is the work of an emperor.'
Since then,
Wèi indeed abandoned Ānyì
and moved the capital to Dàliáng.
Wèi's territory is not even a thousand *lǐ*,
its soldiers do not exceed three hundred thousand.
The land is flat,
The feudal lords connected in all four directions,
with roads and paths extending and converging,
without the barriers of nameless mountains or great rivers.
From Zhèng 鄭 to Liáng 梁,
it was more than two hundred *lǐ*;
with chariots racing and people running,
one arrived before fatigue set in.
Liáng 梁
bordered the territory of Chǔ 楚 to the south,
that of Hán 韓 to the west,
that of Zhào 趙 to the north,
and that of Qí 齊 to the east.
Soldiers garrisoned all around,
and those guarding the watchtowers numbered no fewer than one hundred thousand.
The geographical location of Liáng 梁
made it inherently a battlefield.
Dàliáng 大梁,
is present-day Biànzhōu 汴州.
If Liáng 梁 was allied with Chǔ 楚 to the south,
it would not be allied with Qí 齊,
and Qí 齊 would attack it from the east;
if allied with Qí 齊 to the east,
it would not be allied with Zhào 趙,
and Zhào 趙 would attack it from the north;
if it didn't agree with Hán 韓,
then Hán 韓 would attack it from the west;
if it wasn't close to Chǔ 楚,
then Chǔ would attack its south.
This is what is called the way of "dividing and dismembering."
Moreover, the feudal lords who engage in alliances,
do so to secure their states,
honor their rulers, strengthen their armies, and make their names renowned.
Now, those who form alliances,
under one authority,
swear to be brothers,
sacrificing a white horse to make a covenant on the banks of the Huán River,
to solidify their alliance.
But even close brothers, born of the same parents,
still quarrel over money and possessions.
To rely on the deceitful and treacherous schemes of Sū Qín,
it is already clear that it cannot succeed.
If Your Majesty does not serve Qín,
Qín will send troops to attack beyond the Hé River,
seize Juǎn, Yǎn, and Suānzǎo,
plunder Wèi and take Jìnyáng.
Then Zhào will not move south;
if Zhào does not move south, then Liáng will not move north;
if Liáng does not move north, then the alliance will be broken;
if the alliance is broken, then Your Majesty's kingdom will inevitably be in danger,
and there is no escaping it.
If Qín defeats Hán and then attacks Liáng,
Hán, being fearful of Qín,
Qín and Hán will become one,
and the downfall of Liáng
can be expected immediately.
This is what your servant is worried about for Your Majesty.
In planning for Your Majesty,
nothing is better than serving Qin.
If you serve Qin, then Chǔ and Hán will certainly not dare to move.
Without the worries of Chǔ and Hán,
then Your Majesty can sleep soundly,
and the state will certainly have no worries.
If Your Majesty does not listen to Qin,
and Qin sends down armored soldiers to attack eastward,
even if you then want to serve Qin,
it will not be possible.
Moreover, those who advocate alliance are often eloquent but few are trustworthy,
persuading one feudal lord is to establish the achievement of being enfeoffed as a marquis.
Therefore,
the traveling persuaders of the world
none do not day and night clench their wrists, glare their eyes, and gnash their teeth to speak of the advantages of alliance,
in order to persuade the rulers of men.
If rulers value their eloquence and are swayed by their arguments,
how can they not be deluded?
Your servant has heard:
Accumulated feathers sink a boat,
many light loads break an axle,
the consensus of many mouths melts metal.
Therefore, I wish Your Majesty to carefully consider and make a definite decision."
The King of Wèi thereupon betrayed the alliance treaty,
and requested to make peace with Qin.
Fàn Suī said to King Zhāo of Qin:
"Now, Rǎng Hóu crossing over Hán and Wèi to attack Qí's Gāngshòu,
is not a good plan.
Sending out few troops is not enough to harm Qí,
sending out many troops will harm Qin,
his planning is therefore negligent.
Moreover, King Mǐn of Qí attacked Chǔ to the south,
destroying armies and killing generals.
expanding their territory by a thousand *lǐ* twice,
yet Qí did not gain even an inch of land.
Is it that Qí did not want to gain land?
The situation made it impossible to possess it.
The feudal lords, seeing Qí exhausted,
raised armies to attack it,
resulting in soldiers humiliated and armies weakened.
Thus, the reason Qí was greatly defeated
was because it enriched Hán and Wèi while defeating Chǔ.
This is what is meant by "borrowing bandit soldiers and supplying robber provisions."
Your Majesty would do better to engage in distant diplomacy and near attacks,
gaining an inch, then it is Your Majesty's inch,
gaining a foot, then it is Your Majesty's foot.
Now, to abandon the near and attack the far,
is this not absurd?
In the past,
the state of Zhōngshān was five hundred *lǐ* in extent,
but Zhào alone swallowed it,
achieving success and establishing fame, with benefits accruing to it,
and no one in the world could contend with it.
Now, Hán and Wèi,
are located in the center of the Middle Kingdom and are the pivot of the world.
If Your Majesty wishes to dominate the Central Kingdom and become the pivot of the world,
you should use your power to intimidate Chǔ and Zhào.
If Chǔ is strong, then [Zhào] will attach itself to Chǔ;
if Zhào is strong, then [Chǔ] will attach itself to Zhào.
If both Chǔ and Zhào are attached [to Qin],
then Qí will also be fearful.
If Qí attaches itself, it will surely use humble words and generous gifts to serve Qín.
Once Qí is attached,
then Hán and Wèi can be considered."
The King said:
"Good."
Thereupon, he appointed Suī to be a guest minister,
planned military affairs, and attacked Wèi,
seizing Huái and Xíngqiū.
Qí and Chǔ came to attack Wèi.
The King of Wèi sent people to seek help from Qín,
and their carriages and canopies followed one after another, but Qín's aid did not arrive.
There was a man of Wèi named Táng Suī,
who was over ninety years old.
He said to the King:
"Your old servant requests to go west to persuade the King of Qín,
to order the troops to go out before your servant arrives."
The King bowed twice and sent him off.
Táng Suī arrived in Qín,
and was received by the King of Qín.
The King of Qín said:
"Old man, you have come from afar looking weary,
this must have been very difficult!
Wèi has come to seek help many times,
I know the urgency of Wèi."
Táng Suī said:
"Your Majesty knows the urgency of Wèi, yet the relief troops have not been dispatched.
Your servant secretly believes that the ministers who are employing strategies are incompetent.
Wèi,
is a state of ten thousand chariots,
yet the reason they face west and serve Qín, call themselves an eastern vassal, build imperial palaces, accept caps and sashes, and perform sacrifices in spring and autumn
is that they believe Qín's strength is sufficient to rely on.
Now, the troops of Qí and Chǔ have already joined forces on the borders of Wèi,
and Qín's relief has not been dispatched,
which also makes them rely on the fact that things haven't reached a crisis.
If you make them reach a crisis,
they will then cede territory and form a vertical alliance.
What will Your Majesty save then?
If you must wait until they are in crisis to save them,
this means losing Wèi, an eastern vassal, and strengthening Qí and Chǔ, two formidable forces.
What benefit will Your Majesty gain?"
Thereupon, the King of Qín hastily dispatched troops to Wèi.
Zhāng Yí persuaded King Huái of Chǔ, saying:
"Qín's territory accounts for half the world,
its military strength equals the four states,
it is protected by mountains and rivers,
and its four strategic passes make it secure."
Fàn Suī persuaded King Zhāo of Qín, saying:
"Your Majesty's state
is made secure by its four strategic passes.
To the north, it has Gānquán and Gǔkǒu,
To the south are the Jīng and Wèi Rivers,
to the right are Lǒng and Shǔ,
and to the left are Guān and Bǎn;
capable of mobilizing a million soldiers,
and a thousand war chariots;
if there is advantage, they sally forth to attack,
if there is no advantage, they retreat to defend.
This is the land of a true king.
The people are timid in private quarrels,
but courageous in public warfare,
these are the people of a true king.
If Your Majesty possesses both of these,
and uses them to deal with the feudal lords,
it would be like releasing a Hàn Lú hound to catch a limping rabbit.
You have more than a hundred thousand elite warriors,
a thousand war chariots,
ten thousand cavalry horses,
and grain piled up like hills.
Your laws and decrees are clear,
and your soldiers are secure and content.
Your ruler is wise and strict,
and your generals are intelligent and martial.
Even without sending out armored troops,
you can sweep away the dangers of Chángshān,
and surely break the spine of the world.
Those who submit last to Your Majesty will perish first!
Moreover, those who advocate alliances
are no different from driving a flock of sheep to attack a fierce tiger.
That tigers and sheep
cannot contend is obvious!
Now, Your Majesty sides not with the tigers but with the flock of sheep,
I, your servant, secretly believe that Your Majesty’s plan is flawed.
Among all the powerful states under Heaven,
none are like Qín or Chǔ,
and none are like Chǔ or Qín.
When these two states clash,
their positions cannot both stand.
If Your Majesty does not side with Qín,
and Qín sends down troops to occupy Yíyáng,
the upper territories of Hán will be cut off;
if they send troops down to Hé Dōng and Chéng Gāo,
Hán will surely become a subject.
Then, Liáng will also follow suit like grass in the wind.
If Qín attacks Chǔ from the west,
and Hán attacks from the north,
how can the state altars remain secure?
I have heard:
"Do not challenge those whose armies are inferior;
do not engage in prolonged conflict with those whose grain is inferior."
Qín has Bā and Shǔ in the west,
where large ships accumulate grain,
originating from Wèn Shān,
floating down the river,
reaching Chǔ after more than three thousand lǐ.
A warship carrying soldiers,
one ship carrying five thousand men,
travels three hundred *lǐ* per day.
Although the number of *lǐ* is great,
it does not require the strength of oxen or horses.
In less than ten days,
it will reach the Hàn Pass.
If the Hàn Pass is alarmed, then from the eastern border inward,
all will defend their cities.
Qiánzhōng and the Wū Commandery
